```{r}
#Load all necessary packages
library(sf) # st_read(), st_transform(), st_layers() 
library(janitor) # clean_names()
library(here)
library(tidyverse) #read_csv(), filter(), mutate(), select()
library(terra) # mask(), crop(), rast(), extract()
library(fs)
library(tidyterra) # optional
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
```
```{r}
st_layers("week3/gadm41_CAN.gpkg")
```
Read in the data:

```{r}
# Reading in the main Canada border shape files as a geopackage
canada <- sf::st_read(here("week3", "gadm41_CAN.gpkg"),
                      layer='ADM_ADM_0') 

# Creates a dataframe of the different layers in the Canada border shape files. There are 4 layers total, all of them with multipolygon geometry, and varying set of features and fields
layers <- st_layers(here("week3", "gadm41_CAN.gpkg"))

world_cities <- sf::st_read(here("week3", "World_cities.shp"))

ssp1 <-terra::rast(here("week3", "wc2.1_2.5m_tmax_ACCESS-CM2_ssp126_2081-2100.tif"))

ssp1_mean <- mean(ssp1)

ssp5 <-terra::rast(here("week3", "wc2.1_2.5m_tmax_ACCESS-CM2_ssp585_2081-2100.tif"))

```

```{r}

canadian_cities <- world_cities %>%
```

subtract rasters

```{r}

```

```{r}
names(diff_climate_model)
```
rename and extract data from points

```{r}
month <- c("Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", 
           "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec")

names(diff_climate_model) <- month

canada_city_diff<- terra::extract(diff_climate_model, canadian_cities)

```

Join the extracted data back to the point dataset - make a join ID column in the original point sf and use that to join...

```{r}

canadian_cities_join_ID <- canadian_cities %>%
  dplyr::mutate(join_id= 1:n())
```

```{r}
canadian_cities_join_ID
```
Now join

```{r}

canada_city_diff2 <- canadian_cities_join_ID%>%
  dplyr::left_join(.,
            canada_city_diff,
             by = c("join_id" = "ID"))

```

Drop the geometry and make a facet plot of differences per month

```{r}
# all cities in spain where there is data


city_climate_diff <- canada_city_diff2 %>%
  dplyr::select(c(,16:27))%>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry(.)%>%
  dplyr::as_tibble()

tidy_city_diff <- city_climate_diff %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), 
               names_to="Months", 
               values_to="temp_diff")

# factor column type if for categorical data (factor = levels)
facet_plot <- tidy_city_diff %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Months = factor(Months, levels = c("Jan","Feb","Mar",
                                            "Apr","May","Jun",
                                            "Jul","Aug","Sep",
                                            "Oct","Nov","Dec")))
# Plot faceted histogram
plot<-ggplot(facet_plot, aes(x=temp_diff, na.rm=TRUE))+
  geom_histogram(color="black", binwidth = .1)+
  labs(title="Ggplot2 faceted difference in climate scenarios of max temp", 
       x="Temperature",
       y="Frequency")+
  facet_grid(Months ~ .)+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

plot

```


## Extra

How about taking each climate scenario and plotting the distribution of mean annual (mean of all the months) max temp values for Spanish cities....

* take the temp data
* clip it to Spain 
* take a mean of all the months
* extract the mean of all the months for the 21 cities
* plot it in violin or box plots


```{r}

####### extra analysis####when i assumed it was just a single year not months

ssp1 <-terra::rast(here("homework_3", "wc2.1_2.5m_tmax_ACCESS-CM2_ssp126_2021-2040.tif"))
ssp2 <-terra::rast(here("homework_3", "wc2.1_2.5m_tmax_ACCESS-CM2_ssp245_2021-2040.tif"))
ssp3 <-terra::rast(here("homework_3", "wc2.1_2.5m_tmax_ACCESS-CM2_ssp370_2021-2040.tif"))
ssp5 <-terra::rast(here("homework_3", "wc2.1_2.5m_tmax_ACCESS-CM2_ssp585_2021-2040.tif"))

ssp1mean <- ssp1 %>%
  terra::crop(.,spain)%>%
  terra::mask(.,spain)%>%
  mean(.)

ssp2mean <- ssp2 %>%
  terra::crop(.,spain)%>%
  terra::mask(.,spain)%>%
  mean(.)
  
ssp3mean <- ssp3 %>%
  terra::crop(.,spain)%>%
  terra::mask(.,spain)%>%
  mean(.)
  
ssp5mean <- ssp5 %>%
  terra::crop(.,spain)%>%
  terra::mask(.,spain)%>%
  mean(.)
  
spain_city_ssp1<- terra::extract(ssp1mean, spanish_cities)
spain_city_ssp2<- terra::extract(ssp2mean, spanish_cities)
spain_city_ssp3<- terra::extract(ssp3mean, spanish_cities)
spain_city_ssp5<- terra::extract(ssp5mean, spanish_cities)

spain_city3 <- spanish_cities %>% 
  add_column(ssp1=spain_city_ssp1$mean)%>%
  add_column(ssp2=spain_city_ssp2$mean)%>%
  add_column(ssp3=spain_city_ssp3$mean)%>%
  add_column(ssp5=spain_city_ssp5$mean)

spain_city4 <- spain_city3 %>%
  as_tibble()%>%
  dplyr::select(city_name, ssp1, ssp2, ssp3, ssp5)%>%
  pivot_longer(cols = 2:5,
              names_to = "model",
              values_to = "max_temp"
  )

violin <- ggplot(spain_city4, 
                 aes(x=model, y=max_temp, fill=model)) + # fill=name allow to automatically dedicate a color for each group
  geom_violin(draw_quantiles = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))+
  geom_point()
#geom_jitter(height = 0, width = 0.1)

box <- ggplot(spain_city4, aes(x=model, y=max_temp, fill=model)) + # fill=name allow to automatically dedicate a color for each group
  geom_boxplot()+
  theme_minimal()+
  labs(
    x="Model", 
    y="Climate projection max tempearture")+
  theme(legend.position = "none")

violin
box

# we could also create a violin plot for the whole of spain
# per model or use metro areas. 
```

LECTURE SCRATCH NOTES:

First step - look at the data
Downloaded Spain Country outline from gadm - ssp1, ssp5 
Chose maximum temperature, but can choose any other
Raster data that is continuous - gpkg - specify the specific layer - ADM0 is very broad, ADM4 is localized/region focused
- Columns of temp difference between ssp1 and ssp5 for all cities (ex. in Jan, across all cities in Spain the difference will be -0.1)

Process:
- Read in data
- Check CRS
- Data Wrangling - finish spanish cities
                 - clip rasters (both SSP1 and SSP5) to Spain (optional)
                - subtract rasters

- Extract data - For each city extract the difference
               - Join the difference to the city points
- Join
- Plot
